overview.oneLineTake: Hawkish Fed minutes and a shaky AI trade outweigh solid earnings elsewhere, so expect choppy, downside-leaning trade until rate fears cool.
themes: Fed repricing: minutes show officials expect more rate hikes, and Waller floated a half-point move. Musalem said four more hikes may be needed. The Dow fell 561 points on Wednesday and the S&P 500 broke key support.

AI trade fatigue: Nvidia beat and guided higher, yet the stock sold off on CEO succession and China risk. CoreWeave and other neoclouds slid on debt concerns. Rotation from tech into defensives continues.
Anthropic IPO priced at $83, above the expected range, with strong retail demand. A large supply event for AI exposure.
Rates: the 10-year was 5.10% on Nov 17. Longer-dated yields eased Wednesday on Waller and the minutes. QQQ closed +0.39% while the S&P 500 fell, a mixed tape under the surface.
Earnings dispersion: Target (+7%) and Palo Alto (+7%) rallied on results while tech hardware and software lagged.
risks: Hawkish Fed path with housing already weak: homebuilder sentiment at a 14-year low and record low sales.
Middle East: Iran attacks on Gulf targets, a tanker struck near Hormuz, and the IEA sees no credible path back to normal flows. Record diesel pushed UK inflation to 3.6%.
Nvidia governance and China chip policy, plus the Trump, Xi and Putin summit headlines.
VIX is surging again and the tech outages (banks, FAA) add operational tail risk.

intelligence.summary: Anthropic is set to price its record-breaking IPO today, with trading to start tomorrow. That's well above the $1.4 trillion the company would be worth at the top of its proposed IPO price range. The perpetual futures contracts give investors an early read on speculative appetite, though those willing to place the bets aren't necessarily the ones who will buy the shares. intelligence.headline: Apollo's Rowan Says AI Buildout Could Demand $8 Trillion
intelligence.summary: "In three to four years, we will go from a bond market dominated by the 10 largest banks to one where six of the top 10 issuers are technology companies. It is a transformation we have never seen before," said Marc Rowan, CEO of Apollo Global Management. The AI buildout could demand as much as $8 trillion of financing, Rowan said at a conference this week.
